html:
A city on the high plain of central Anatolia, in Turkey, known in ancient times as Iconium. It was the capital of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum and is the city of the poet Rumi.

Iconium was an old Phrygian and then Greek and Roman town, and the apostle Paul preached there. After the Seljuk victory at Manzikert in 1071, Turks settled across Anatolia. When crusaders and Byzantines took their first capital, Nicaea, in 1097, the Seljuk sultans of Rum moved to Konya.

It was their capital for nearly two centuries. From it Sultan Kilij Arslan II marched to destroy a Byzantine army at Myriokephalon in 1176. In the 1200s the sultans filled the city with mosques, madrasas and palaces, and built caravan inns along the trade roads out of it.

The family of Rumi fled the Mongols and came to Konya around 1228. He taught and wrote his great poems there and died in 1273. His followers founded the Mevlevi order, the "whirling dervishes", with its centre at his green-domed tomb. After Mongol defeat the Seljuk state faded, the Karamanid emirate ruled Konya, and the Ottomans took it in the 1400s. The Mevlevi lodge is now a museum.
sum: A city on the high plain of central Anatolia, in Turkey, known in ancient times as Iconium. It was the capital of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum and is the city of the poet Rumi.
